knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the method-of-moments move for constructing an estimator?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the MoM construction (estimator, not interval).
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MoM equates moments and solves for a point estimator. MLE is a different construction, and a confidence interval is not an estimator in the MoM sense.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Equate sample moments to population moments and solve for the parameter.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing MoM with MLE, or treating a CI as the MoM estimator.

choices.label: Match sample moments to population moments (as functions of parameters) and solve to construct a point estimator of the parameter.
Maximise the likelihood; the maximiser is called the method-of-moments estimator by definition.
Construct a confidence interval for the parameter; the interval itself is the method-of-moments estimator.
Choose any convenient formula for θ̂; method of moments means having a closed form, regardless of how it was derived.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: Poisson MoM mean
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Six independent monthly claim counts are modelled as Poisson(λ): 2, 1, 3, 0, 4, 2. Enter the method-of-moments estimate of λ.
knowledge_checks.body: Evaluate λ̂_MoM = x̄ on the stated sample.
hints: For Poisson(λ), the first-moment equation gives λ̂_MoM = x̄.
Sum the six counts and divide by n = 6.
knowledge_checks.explanation: E[X] = λ implies λ̂_MoM = x̄. The sample mean is (2 + 1 + 3 + 0 + 4 + 2)/6 = 12/6 = 2, so λ̂_MoM = 2 claims per month.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reporting the sum Σxᵢ = 12 as λ̂, or treating a variance match as a required second MoM step for one-parameter Poisson.
success_criteria: Uses the sample mean as MoM for the Poisson mean λ.

worked_example.title: MoM for Poisson claim counts
worked_example.problem_statement: Six independent monthly claim counts on a small commercial book are modelled as Poisson(λ): 2, 1, 3, 0, 4, 2. Construct the method-of-moments estimator of λ and evaluate it on this sample.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Equate the Poisson mean λ to the sample mean before computing.

steps.label: Moment equation
steps.explanation: Poisson has E[X] = λ, so MoM matches λ to the sample mean.

steps.label: Evaluate on the sample
steps.explanation: Substitute the observed counts into x̄.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Equating λ to the sample variance (here also 2 by chance) as if that were a second-moment MoM step required for one-parameter Poisson, or reporting Σxᵢ = 12 as the estimate of λ.
